html:
The Ngunnawal, also spelt Ngunawal, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southern tablelands of New South Wales and the area of today's Canberra.

Their neighbours were the Gundungurra to the northeast, the Ngarigo of the high country, the Yuin on the coast and the Wiradjuri to the west. Which people were the traditional owners of the Canberra area is still argued; the Ngambri make a rival claim.

Settlers brought stock onto the Limestone Plains in the 1820s. In 1908 the area was chosen for the new federal capital of Australia, and Parliament moved to Canberra in 1927.
sum: The Ngunnawal, also spelt Ngunawal, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southern tablelands of New South Wales and the area of today's Canberra.
